title: reading a Result's runtime discriminant is not one of the five acts that discharge the must-use rule
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Matching and Transformation': 'A Result MUST be treated as a must-use value. A source program MUST NOT silently discard a Result without returning, matching, transforming, inspecting, or unwrapping it.' The sentence that settles whether a `.ok` read is the 'inspecting' act is one section earlier, in 'Compiler-Owned Modules': `smthrs/result` 'is the lowering target: emitted code imports it... The compiler links it directly, `!` and `expect` are rejected inside it, and its public API is instance methods.' `ok` is a property of the lowering target's runtime classes, not an instance method, so it is not on the authoring surface at all — and the page's own inspection group is `isOk isError match`, three methods, of which 07-must-consume/every-listed-consumption-form-is-accepted already pins `isError()` as the inspecting form. WHAT THE CASE PINS is the binding's SMITHERS1302: `outcome` is read three times and consumed none of them. VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, on both backends, one variable at a time. (1) The divergence is NOT only in the must-use walk — it is in the authored `Result` TYPE. Discharge the obligation another way first (`const name = outcome.unwrapOr("-")` above the tag read) and the reference reports a stock `TS2339` on `.ok` while the fork compiles and runs, so the reference's Result has no such member and the fork's does. (2) `outcome.value` and `outcome.error` read WITHOUT a `.ok` guard are `TS2339` on BOTH backends: the fork admits the discriminant only, and the payload halves become readable only once it narrows. (3) `isOk()` narrows on NEITHER backend — `if (outcome.isOk()) { return [outcome.value] }` is `TS2339` at `.value` on both — so `.ok` is the only narrowing spelling either implementation has, which is why this reads as a capability rather than a slip. (4) THE LABEL WAS A RED HERRING. This defect arrived reported as `outer: { … break outer; … }`. 38 labeled-form probes were measured across labeled blocks, labeled statements, labeled while/do/for/for-of/switch, bare and labeled `break`/`continue`, nested and duplicate labels, and labels inside arrows, nested functions and object methods: the two backends agree on every one of them, and wrapping THIS program in a labeled block changes neither backend's answer. The label was incidental to the finder's probe; the rule that fires is must-consume on a binding, not anything label-aware. This case is therefore NOT a member of the `statementMayFallThrough` class that 02-unwrap-propagation/postfix-bang-in-a-labeled-statement-body-is-accepted records. THE CONSEQUENCE, measured: the fork prints `zoe` — it extracted the ERROR value and read a field off it with no `!`, no `match`, no `unwrapOr` and no `expect`. failures.mdx, 'Authorability' states that 'the language has no form that extracts the error from a Result' and marks 'Whether Smithers gains an error-extraction form' **Open**, so the shape the fork built on top of the tag is an Open decision it has settled on its own. This case pins only the must-use consequence, which is locked; the error-extraction spelling belongs to the decision ledger owner.

xfail.reason: THE FORK ACCEPTS, COMPILES AND RUNS THIS PROGRAM (exit 0, prints `zoe`). It is a fail-open, and it is deliberate rather than a gap: `compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt`'s `collectResultInspectionMembers` indexes the prelude Result variants' `ok` property — and the `value`/`error` readonly constructor parameters — into `resultInspectionDecls`, and `preludeSymbols.resultInspection` treats an authored read that resolves to one of those declarations as a discharge of the must-consume obligation. `compiler/fork_mustconsume_test.go`, 'compiler-owned Result inspection consumes the binding', asserts exactly this behaviour, and `compiler/fork_internal_lowering_test.go` authors `if (outcome.ok) { return "ok:" + outcome.value }` in a lowering fixture. DELETING THE `ok` ENTRY WOULD NOT CLOSE THIS, which is why the marker is filed instead of an edit: on the fork the authored `Result` IS the union of its two runtime classes `SmithersOk`/`SmithersErr`, so `outcome.ok` would still typecheck after the discharge was removed. Verified: with the obligation discharged by `unwrapOr` first, the fork still compiles and runs the tag read while the reference reports `TS2339` — a difference in the two backends' Result type surfaces, not in their ownership walks. Closing it means giving `.sm` a Result surface that is not the fork's runtime representation, which is a design change and moves an Open decision (failures.mdx, 'Authorability'), so it is recorded here rather than taken by a lane. The reference's own surface is `RESULT_MEMBER_SIGNATURES` in `poc/src/language/semantic.ts`, which declares fifteen instance methods and no properties; `compiler/fork_result_member_surface_test.go` already pins the two backends' METHOD lists to each other and would not have seen this, because `ok` is on neither list.
